# Awesome AI on Your Laptop

Find local AI apps for document chat, transcription, dictation, image editing and coding, with setup requirements, source links and practical caveats.

**17 curated entries** · [Browse by task](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/README.md#browse-by-task) · [Suggest a project](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/issues/new?template=suggest-project.yml) · [JSON catalog](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/catalog.json) · [Agent index](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/llms.txt)

Choose a useful task, compare the setup, then follow the original project. This collection covers desktop apps and a small set of supporting tools for Windows, macOS and Linux. Local execution is configuration-specific; cloud options are called out where relevant.

## Start here

| If you want to... | Explore | Why it belongs |
|---|---|---|
| Chat with a downloaded model | [Jan](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/projects/jan.md) | A graphical starting point for local model use. |
| Ask questions about documents | [AnythingLLM](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/projects/anythingllm.md) | A document workspace with configurable providers. |
| Dictate into another app | [OpenWhispr](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/projects/openwhispr.md) | Hotkey-based voice input with a local mode. |
| Transcribe an existing recording | [Buzz](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/projects/buzz.md) | A dedicated transcription interface. |
| Enlarge an image | [Upscayl](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/projects/upscayl.md) | A focused image upscaler; check Vulkan support. |

## What is checked

Entries distinguish documentation review from hands-on testing. The initial collection is **documentation-reviewed**: source material was inspected, but these applications have not all been installed or benchmarked by QuicqDev. Each project card records its sources, review date, requirements and a limitation.

Hardware requirements depend on model, quantization, context length and workload. We do not infer RAM needs from parameter counts. Application code, model weights and optional hosted services can have different licenses or costs. Check the linked upstream terms for the configuration you choose.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I use these apps without a paid API key?

Several entries provide local inference after downloading software and models. Optional cloud models or features may require a paid key. Check the project card and upstream configuration rather than treating the whole application as free to run.

### Will these work on an 8 GB or 16 GB laptop?

There is no universal answer. Model size, quantization, context length, input resolution, GPU memory and operating system all matter. The collection links to requirements rather than assigning unsupported memory guarantees. Reproducible hardware reports are welcome.

### Does local AI mean no network traffic?

Not automatically. Downloads, update checks, optional cloud providers and custom extensions can use the network. Use a documented local configuration; this collection has not audited network behavior.

### Are all entries open source?

The collection prioritizes inspectable projects but includes local tools with custom or mixed terms, explicitly noted in their cards. Code licenses and model licenses must be checked separately.

## How to contribute

Add a useful project, correct an outdated entry, or submit a reproducible compatibility report. Edit `catalog.json` and run `python scripts/build.py`; the README, project cards and agent index are generated from that source. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for selection criteria and the field format.

Automated checks validate the catalog on changes and check external links weekly. A reachable link does not establish that software works, is secure, or fits your hardware. Failed and inconclusive checks need review; metadata checks never advance an editorial review date.

## For agents and search tools

Read the [structured catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/main/catalog.json), its [schema](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/catalog.schema.json), or the compact [llms.txt index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/main/llms.txt). Each entry has a stable ID, category, use case, prerequisites, caveat, evidence level and source URLs. Cite the upstream project for its capabilities and this collection for editorial comparisons.

`llms.txt` is a navigation aid, not a promise of inclusion in any search engine or model response. Unknown requirements remain unknown; documentation-reviewed entries must not be described as personally tested.

# Docling: Convert PDFs into structured text before indexing or summarizing them

Document conversion toolkit with structured export for downstream AI applications.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/README.md#documents-to-data)

|---|---|
| Category | Documents to data |
| Use case | Convert PDFs into structured text before indexing or summarizing them. |
| Requirements | Python environment and the model assets required by the chosen conversion pipeline. |
| Caveat | A parsing result is not a factual summary; complex layouts and scanned documents need output review. |

Terminal coding assistant that works with local or cloud language models.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/README.md#coding-and-model-runners)

# llama.cpp: Control a local model server and its inference settings directly

C/C++ inference engine with CLI and server interfaces for supported models.

[Upstream project](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) · [Back to collection](https://github.com/QuicqDev/awesome-ai-on-your-laptop/blob/main/README.md#coding-and-model-runners)

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Category | Coding and model runners |
| Use case | Control a local model server and its inference settings directly. |
| Requirements | Compatible build and model file; supports CPU and multiple acceleration backends. |
| Caveat | More configuration is exposed than in a desktop app; quantization and context size change resource needs. |
| Evidence | documentation-reviewed |
| Documentation reviewed | 2026-09-12 |
